The Verify phase sends remaining findings to adversarial agents that attempt to refute each claim by reading the actual code—only findings that survive skeptical scrutiny are marked isReal=true. Finally, the Synthesize phase produces a prioritized overhaul plan grouping confirmed bugs into fix batches that touch related files together and selecting 5-8 small-to-medium effort feature enhancements grounded in existing services, favoring integration wins and HIG polish over new subsystems. # Handoff.md — SwiftMandarin: Bilingual + Multi-Provider AI Overhaul

**Last Updated (UTC):** 2026-06-13
**Status:** In Progress (iter 9 — native-language tailoring)
**Current Focus (latest):** Interface-language-driven tailoring: when the UI is 中文 the user is treated as a native Mandarin speaker learning English (AI explanations written in Mandarin; saved words show ENGLISH as the big headline with Mandarin small; English TTS emphasis) and vice versa for English UI. Full audit + plan: docs/language-direction-audit.md (11-agent parallel map + completeness critic, 2026-06-13).
**Prior Focus:** Full-app audit + overhaul: 18 verified bug fixes, integration wins (unified history/stats, pinyin position, provider test connection), zero-warning builds, bilingual READMEs — see Updates iter 8 (2026-06-10).
**Prior Focus:** Full UI localization (English ⇄ 中文) with a runtime in-app language toggle — see Updates iter 5 (2026-06-07).
**Prior Focus:** Four-part overhaul — (A) fix photo OCR Chinese gibberish/language lock, (B) multi-provider cloud AI with API-fetched model lists, (C) photo→AI cleanup toggle, (D) make the app fully bilingual (dual narration + learner-mode toggle).

## 1) Request & Context
- **A — Photo OCR bug:** Photo upload "often produces gibberish," "cannot switch languages," "stuck on detecting English, can't read Mandarin."
- **B — Provider expansion:** Add OpenAI, Claude (Anthropic), Deepseek, Doubao, Qwen, Kimi, Zhipu, Minimax. Pull each provider's available models via API.
- **C — Deep AI integration:** A settings toggle that routes an uploaded photo to an AI model for cleanup/structuring, returning cleaned text into the app.
- **D — Bilingual:** App must serve English-speakers-learning-Mandarin AND Mandarin-speakers-learning-English (and both). Add English narration alongside Mandarin for the selected word, and a settings toggle that flips the app between English-centric and Mandarin-centric, adapting features.

**Environment:** Xcode 26.3, iOS/macOS/visionOS **26.2** deploy targets, Swift 5 mode, single target `SwiftMandarin`, sandboxed (`ENABLE_APP_SANDBOX=YES`), generated Info.plist. One SPM dep: `ollama-swift 1.8.0`. State = `@Observable @MainActor` singletons over UserDefaults JSON. No Keychain, no network entitlement yet.

## 2) Verified Root Causes (from full-codebase read + 9-agent comprehension workflow)
**A (compounding 4-stage failure):**
1. `PhotoTextRecognitionService.swift:204` — `recognitionLanguages = ["en-US","en-GB","zh-Hans","zh-Hant"]` English-first; `automaticallyDetectsLanguage` never set; no per-call override → genuinely "cannot switch languages."
2. `:207` — `usesLanguageCorrection = true` unconditionally → English autocorrect mangles Chinese into Latin gibberish.
3. `:45-72` (+ dup in `PhotoTranslateView:601`, `CameraScannerView:123`) — English-centric cleaner joins with spaces / English punctuation regex → corrupts spaceless Chinese.
4. `PhotoTranslateView:573-598` — language detection runs AFTER OCR on already-garbled text; non-Chinese falls back to English; `TextRecognitionResult.language` hardwired `nil`.
Secondary: `CameraScannerView:40` `.text()` no language hint; `VNImageRequestHandler` ignores orientation; `Character.isChineseCharacter` misses ranges.

**B:** `AIProvider` enum has only `.appleIntelligence`/`.ollama`; `AIModelSettings` Ollama-shaped, no API key storage; `OllamaService` (third-party `Ollama.Client`) can't reach cloud (hardcoded `/api/*`, no auth header). Exhaustive switches at `AIModelSettings:124,134`, `AIWordExplanationService:395,411`, `MacOSSettingsView:280`, `MoreView:471`; availability hardcoded in `ShortcutHelpers:95`, `AIWordExplanationView:27`.

**C:** Seam = `PhotoTranslateView.loadAndProcessImage` between `recognizeText(from:)` (`:508`) and `sourceText = result.cleanedText` (`:512`). No toggle, no image-capable provider today.

**D:** Narration single-language (`WordDetailPopover:272` Chinese only; `EnglishWordDetailSheet:184` English only). No learner-mode concept; defaults hardcoded English-first (`TranslationDirection`, `TranslationState`).

## 3) Plan & Decomposition
**Group 1 — Foundations:** entitlements network.client; `KeychainHelper`; `AppPreferences` (LearnerMode, PhotoScanLanguage, dualNarration); extend `AIProvider` + per-provider metadata + per-provider config/keys in `AIModelSettings` (generalized switches via `default:`); `CloudAIService` (URLSession; OpenAI-compatible + Anthropic; listModels w/ fallback; chat; vision; translate).
**Group 2 — OCR (A):** robust CJK-ratio-first detector + widened CJK in `ChineseTextAnalyzer`; parameterized recognition + Chinese-aware clean + language populated + orientation in `PhotoTextRecognitionService`; `.text(languages:)` in `CameraScannerView`; scan-language override UI + AI-cleanup hook + Chinese-aware processing in `PhotoTranslateView`.
**Group 3 — AI routing (B/C):** cloud dispatch + `cleanupRecognizedText` + tolerant JSON in `AIWordExplanationService`; cloud availability in `ShortcutHelpers`, `AIWordExplanationView`.
**Group 4 — Settings UI (B/C/D):** shared `AIProviderConfigView`; wire into `MacOSSettingsView` + `MoreView`; add learner-mode + photo-cleanup toggles.
**Group 5 — Narration (D):** dual narration in `WordDetailPopover` + `EnglishWordDetailSheet`.

## 4) Requirements → Acceptance Checks
| Req | Check | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| A | Scan Chinese textbook → Chinese chars recognized, not gibberish; manual 中文/English/Auto switch works | macOS build + manual |
| B | Settings shows 10 providers; entering key + Refresh lists models from API | build + manual |
| C | Toggle ON → photo OCR text cleaned by AI before display | build + manual |
| D | Word detail shows both 朗读中文 + Read English; learner-mode toggle flips defaults | build + manual |
| All | `xcodebuild` macOS Debug succeeds, zero errors | pending |

## 5) Decisions
- Cloud clients via **URLSession** (no new SPM deps). All Chinese providers are OpenAI-compatible; Anthropic uses `/v1/messages` + `x-api-key`.
- API keys in **Keychain** (generic password), never UserDefaults.
- Exhaustive `AIProvider` switches converted to use `default:` (cloud) so future providers don't break compilation.
- `live model list` falls back to curated `defaultModels` per provider when the `/models` endpoint is absent/blocked.
- Learner mode adjusts defaults (direction, scan language) and is additive — never removes capability; dual narration always offered when both languages available.

## 6) Progress Ledger
- [x] G1 foundations — entitlements `network.client`; `KeychainHelper`; `AppPreferences`; extended `AIProvider` (10 providers) + per-provider keys/models in `AIModelSettings`; `CloudAIService` (URLSession, OpenAI + Anthropic, vision, model listing).
- [x] G2 OCR (A) — robust CJK-ratio detector + widened CJK in `ChineseTextAnalyzer`; parameterized recognition language + Chinese-aware cleaning + language carried + EXIF orientation in `PhotoTextRecognitionService`; `.text(languages:)` + language-aware cleaning in `CameraScannerView`; scan-language menu + "重新识别" + AI-cleanup hook + Chinese-aware processing in `PhotoTranslateView`.
- [x] G3 AI routing (B/C) — cloud dispatch + `generateExplanationWithCloud` + `cleanupRecognizedText` + tolerant JSON in `AIWordExplanationService`; `isAnyProviderAvailable` in `ShortcutHelpers` + `AIWordExplanationView`.
- [x] G4 settings UI (B/C/D) — shared `AIProviderConfigView`; wired into macOS `AISettingsTab` + iOS `AISettingsDetailView`; generalized `statusColor` switches (`default:` cloud); learner-mode + dual-narration sections; AI-photo-cleanup toggles.
- [x] G5 narration (D) — dual-language narration in `WordDetailPopover` (中文 + EN) and `EnglishWordDetailSheet` (English + 中文).
- [x] build green — macOS Debug ✅, iOS Simulator Debug ✅ (only 2 pre-existing warnings). Logic check: 9/9 detector+cleaning assertions pass.

## 8) Verification Summary
- `xcodebuild -scheme SwiftMandarin -destination 'platform=macOS' -configuration Debug` → **BUILD SUCCEEDED**.
- `xcodebuild ... -destination 'generic/platform=iOS Simulator' ...` → **BUILD SUCCEEDED**.
- Standalone Swift check of `detectLanguageRobust` + Chinese whitespace cleaning: **9/9 passed** (pure/traditional/mixed Chinese → chinese; English/English-dominant → english; despacing preserves Latin spaces).
- Learner-mode → direction wiring confirmed via `TranslateView.applyDefaultDirectionIfNeeded()` reading the `defaultDirection` UserDefaults key updated by `LearnerMode.didSet`.
- Not yet runtime-tested with a live cloud API key or a real Chinese photo (requires user secrets / GUI). Behavior reasoned + compile-verified.

## 10) Updates
- 2026-06-13 (iter 10 — native-language tailoring by interface language): The interface language now doubles as the user's NATIVE language and re-orients the whole app: 中文 UI → native Mandarin speaker learning English (AI explanations written in 简体中文; saved words / phrases / flashcards / popovers show the ENGLISH side as the big headline with the Mandarin gloss small; pinyin hidden — it's a learner aid, not native furniture; TTS leads with English); English UI → the historic English-speaker-learning-Chinese behavior, unchanged. Audit: 11-agent parallel map + completeness critic over all 19.6k lines → docs/language-direction-audit.md (findings incl. critic-caught gaps: Ollama/cloud prompt paths, missing LocalizationManager↔learnerMode link, Chinese-POS stats breakage; plus deliberate rejections — `Text("…")` literals already localize via catalog, CSV column swap would break import round-trips). **Core abstraction:** `LocalizationManager.nativeIsChinese`/`learningIsChinese` + `AppLanguage.persisted` (nonisolated snapshot for App Intents); language toggle now syncs `AppPreferences.learnerMode` (and first-launch learnerMode derives from UI language); `SavedTerm.chineseSide/englishSide/headlineText/glossText/showsPinyin` — sides are CONTENT-DETECTED (`String.containsCJK`, new in ChineseTextAnalyzer.swift) because the `chinese` headword field can hold English (photo/grading flows); `SpeechService.speakAuto` picks the voice by content. **AI explanations (all 3 provider paths):** `ExplanationDirection` (wordIsChinese from content, explainInChinese from UI language, cacheToken so language toggles never serve stale cross-language cache); FoundationModels @Generable structs re-guided direction-neutral (ExampleSentence.sentence/pinyin/translation, RelatedWord.word, Collocation.phrase); Ollama schema + cloud JSON instructions parameterized; decoder accepts new keys with legacy chinese/english fallback; example/collocation word-filtering now checks the right field; `extractVocabulary` meanings in the user's native language; `gradeWorkbook` explanations/summary in native language, fullSentence/vocab term in the learning language (`spokenEnglish`→`spokenSentence`, spoken via speakAuto). **UI:** VocabularyView row/sheet/inspector headline-swap + conditional pinyin + direction-aware translate-fetch (translate(headword, sourceIsChinese: headword.containsCJK)) + alphabetical sort on the visible headword + "headword font size" labels; AIWordExplanationView renders sentence/pinyin-if-any/translation + per-example speakAuto button; LearnView flashcards quiz the learning language on the front (incl. saved-term side mapping); PhrasesView rows/detail flip + localized category headers (LocalizedStringKey(category.name) — keys existed); WordDetailPopover headline/definition/TTS-order/copy flip; EnglishWordDetailSheet inverts for English UI (Chinese headline + pinyin, Mandarin TTS first); TranslateView showEnglishFirst forced in 中文 UI; HistoryTabView rows learning-language-first (entry extension with direction-derived sides); TranslatedScreenshotOverlayView speakAuto. **Storage:** workbook `saveVocabItem` and photo `saveExtractedVocab` now key the saved entry on the LEARNING-language term (was: forced-Chinese headword — backwards for 中文 users and silently DROPPED English-passage items lacking CJK; English terms no longer translated-to-Chinese just to make a key); `ScreenshotTranslationStore.targetLanguage` defaults to the native language (set in init — comprehension aid). **Intents:** SavedTermEntity/PhraseEntity display titles = learning-language side (via AppLanguage.persisted, content-detected); GetRandomPhraseIntent speaks/copies the learning side; GetLearningStatsIntent labels localized (4 new %lld keys); TranslateScreenshotsIntent gained `.appLanguage` default target case. **Guards:** PartOfSpeechCategory.categorize matches Chinese POS labels (名词/动词/形容词/副词/代词/介词/连词/叹词/量词/助词 + traditional variants, compounds checked first) so Mandarin AI output doesn't bucket to "Other" in Stats; TranslationDirection.placeholder localized. **Catalog:** +11 keys with zh-Hans (612 total): Read the full sentence aloud, headword font size ×2, stats ×4, Enter English text…/输入中文… (en), Translate into your native language, screenshots-target description. (7) `TranslateScreenshotsIntent` images param dropped supportedContentTypes (typed variant is 18-only, legacy variant deprecation-warns on macOS). (8) About screen text/icon updated; 3 new catalog keys (zh-Hans). READMEs: requirements iOS 17+, per-version feature matrix (EN+zh). **iOS-17 user model:** translation features all work via configured AI provider (clear error guiding to Settings → AI otherwise); 18–25 get Apple translation in the three main views but AI fallback for word-taps/screenshot/Shortcuts (standalone session init is 26-only); 26+ unchanged. NOTE: only the iOS 26.3 simulator runtime is installed locally — the port is compile-verified at target 17 but not runtime-tested on an iOS 17 device/simulator. Also: Xcode (open during the session) re-added 4 duplicate Sources entries to the pbxproj; removed again — close Xcode or re-check `grep "in Sources" project.pbxproj` before committing pbxproj changes.
- 2026-06-10 (iter 8 — full audit + ship-ready overhaul): Ran a 58-agent audit workflow (12 subsystem/dimension finders → 45 adversarial verifications → synthesis): 113 raw findings, 18 confirmed bugs, 27 refuted. **Bug fixes:** (1) `gradeWorkbook` no longer silently returns "0/0" — decoded-but-empty results now throw a localized, actionable error; 831	    func extractVocabulary(
832	        fromPhotoText text: String,
833	        imageData: Data? = nil,
834	        sourceIsChinese: Bool
835	    ) async throws -> [ExtractedVocabItem] {
836	        let trimmed = text.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
837	        guard !trimmed.isEmpty else { return [] }
838	
839	        let settings = AIModelSettings.shared
840	        let provider = settings.effectiveProvider
841	
842	        let langDesc = sourceIsChinese ? "Chinese (中文)" : "English"
843	        let readingNote = sourceIsChinese
844	            ? "the Hanyu pinyin with tone marks (ā á ǎ à)"
845	            : "a short pronunciation hint (may be an empty string)"
846	        // Meanings are written in the learner's NATIVE language (= the
847	        // interface language) so the study list reads naturally for them.
848	        let nativeDesc = LocalizationManager.shared.nativeIsChinese
849	            ? "Simplified Chinese (简体中文)"
850	            : "English"
851	
852	        let system = """
853	        You extract the most important vocabulary a language learner should study from a passage.
854	        The passage is in \(langDesc). Return ONLY a JSON object of this exact shape:

1034	    /// Decode a grading response, repairing common LLM JSON mistakes if needed.
1035	    private static func decodeGrading(_ json: String) -> GradingResult? {
1036	        guard let data = extractJSONObject(from: json) else { return nil }
1037	        if let result = try? JSONDecoder().decode(GradingResult.self, from: data) { return result }
1038	        // Retry after a string-aware repair (inserts missing commas, drops trailing ones).
1039	        let repaired = repairJSON(String(data: data, encoding: .utf8) ?? "")
1040	        if let rdata = repaired.data(using: .utf8),
1041	           let result = try? JSONDecoder().decode(GradingResult.self, from: rdata) {
1042	            return result
1043	        }
1044	        return nil
1045	    }

1047	    /// Repair the most common LLM JSON errors without corrupting string values:
1048	    /// insert missing commas between adjacent values and remove trailing commas.
1049	    /// Tracks string/escape state so braces inside text are left untouched.
1050	    static func repairJSON(_ s: String) -> String {
1051	        let chars = Array(s)
1052	        var out: [Character] = []
1053	        out.reserveCapacity(chars.count)
1054	        var inString = false
1055	        var escaped = false
1056	        var i = 0
1057	        while i < chars.count {
1058	            let c = chars[i]
1059	            out.append(c)
1060	
1061	            var valueJustClosed = false
1062	            if inString {
1063	                if escaped { escaped = false }
1064	                else if c == "\\" { escaped = true }
1065	                else if c == "\"" { inString = false; valueJustClosed = true }
1066	            } else if c == "\"" {
1067	                inString = true
1068	            } else if c == "}" || c == "]" {
1069	                valueJustClosed = true
1070	            }
1071	
1072	            // A value just ended outside a string. If the next significant char
1073	            // begins a new value/key with no comma between, insert one. (A key's
1074	            // closing quote is followed by ':', so it never triggers this.)
1075	            if valueJustClosed, !inString {
1076	                var j = i + 1
1077	                while j < chars.count, chars[j] == " " || chars[j] == "\n" || chars[j] == "\t" || chars[j] == "\r" {
1078	                    j += 1
1079	                }
1080	                if j < chars.count {
1081	                    let next = chars[j]
1082	                    if next == "{" || next == "[" || next == "\"" {
1083	                        out.append(",")
1084	                    }
1085	                }
1086	            }
1087	            i += 1
1088	        }
1089	        var result = String(out)
1090	        // Remove any trailing commas before a closing brace/bracket.
1091	        result = result.replacingOccurrences(of: ",\\s*}", with: "}", options: .regularExpression)
1092	        result = result.replacingOccurrences(of: ",\\s*]", with: "]", options: .regularExpression)
1093	        return result
1094	    }

content.content:
=== EXECUTIVE SUMMARY ===
SwiftMandarin is a feature-rich, ambitious SwiftUI Mandarin-learning app whose breadth (8 tabs, 10-provider AI abstraction, on-device + cloud translation, photo OCR, screenshot stitching, workbook grading, spaced repetition, bilingual UI) outpaces the robustness of its foundations. The codebase is functional but carries three structural risks that should be treated as release-blockers. (1) PERSISTENCE FRAGILITY: every persisted model uses synthesized Codable with no CodingKeys, no schemaVersion, and no defaulting (confirmed by grep across Models/). The PersistentCodableStore .backup is the SAME schema, so any future non-optional field throws keyNotFound on BOTH decode paths and silently wipes all user vocabulary/progress/history on update. Collection decode is all-or-nothing, so one corrupt row drops the whole array. This is the single highest-leverage area to harden. (2) CORRECTNESS BUGS IN CORE FLOWS: the History store records the UI-toggle direction instead of the actually-translated direction (confirmed TranslateView.swift:889 vs :959/:975), corrupting every cross-direction entry and everything derived from it; the audio pipeline spawns a non-Sendable AVAudioPCMBuffer into a per-buffer Task (use-after-free + reordering), and the sample-rate converter re-feeds the same buffer forever; screenshot stitching mixes a padded source stride with an unpadded render buffer, corrupting overlap detection; CSV round-trip is lossy for any multi-line field. (3) IA/DISCOVERABILITY DEBT: on the now-live iOS 17 path the legacy TabView emits 8 tabs with no compact-width gating (confirmed ContentView.swift:148-179), so tabs 5-8 — including the app's OWN More tab — collapse under the system More overflow, a confusing collision. The genuinely valuable workbook-grading feature is reachable through exactly one buried sheet (PhotoTranslateView.swift:210) and nothing else. The More tab is a 601-line catch-all with a duplicate divergent History screen, dead settings, a placeholder App Store ID, and a privacy link pointing at apple.com. Strategically, the app is one solid refactor of the data layer, the information architecture, and a unified translation/learning-direction model away from being genuinely excellent. Concurrency safety is also unverified by the compiler (SWIFT_STRICT_CONCURRENCY is unset), masking the audio races. Recommend: freeze new features, ship the persistence envelope + the history-direction fix + the audio-buffer fix first, then execute the IA consolidation (5 tabs + real More hub) and a single source-of-truth learning-direction model.

=== TOP ISSUES ===
1. [critical] Schema evolution will silently wipe all user data on the next model change
   why: All persisted models (SavedTerm, CardProgress, DailyActivity, history) use synthesized Codable with no schemaVersion/CodingKeys/decode defaults (verified: grep finds none in Models/). PersistentCodableStore.load decodes the whole collection at once and the .backup is the same schema, so adding any non-optional stored property throws keyNotFound on BOTH the primary and backup decode, and load() returns nil — every saved word, flashcard, streak, and history entry is dropped on update. One corrupt element also discards the entire array.
   fix: Introduce a versioned envelope {schemaVersion:Int, data:T} in save/load. Decode tolerantly: give new fields explicit decodeIfPresent defaults via custom init(from:), and add a per-element resilient decoder (decode [FailableDecodable<Element>], keep successes, log/drop only the truly-corrupt rows). Ship this BEFORE any further model changes so existing 0.x payloads survive the upgrade.
2. [high] History records the UI-toggle direction, not the translated direction — corrupts every cross-direction entry
   why: Confirmed: triggerTranslation computes actualDirection = detectedTranslationDirection from input content (TranslateView.swift:889), but performTranslation (line 959) and triggerAITranslation (line 923) snapshot directionSnapshot = sharedState.direction (the UI toggle) and write THAT into handleCompletedTranslation (line 975). When the toggle says EN→中 but the user types Chinese, the engine correctly returns English yet history stores direction=englishToChinese. TranslationHistoryEntry.chineseText/.englishText key off direction, so source and target are mislabeled through History, restore, and any term saved from a restored entry.
   fix: Thread the detected direction through: compute actualDirection = detectedTranslationDirection in performTranslation/triggerAITranslation and pass that (not sharedState.direction) to both the guard comparison and handleCompletedTranslation's direction: argument. Keep the source-text snapshot guard.
3. [high] Audio tap captures a non-Sendable AVAudioPCMBuffer into a per-buffer Task (use-after-free + reordered/garbled audio)
   why: SpeechRecognitionService.swift:440-446 spawns Task { await self.processAudioBuffer(buffer) } per tap callback. AVAudioEngine reclaims that buffer once the closure returns, so the async read touches recycled memory; tens of unstructured Tasks/sec hop to the MainActor with no FIFO guarantee (frames reorder), and in-flight Tasks outlive stop()/removeTap, yielding into a finished continuation. Separately the sample-rate converter input block (lines 473-476) always returns the same buffer with .haveData, so the converter can loop/duplicate frames and never signals end-of-stream.
   fix: Do conversion synchronously inside the tap and call inputContinuation?.yield(...) directly (the continuation is Sendable/thread-safe); never spawn a Task per buffer. If a hop is unavoidable, deep-copy the buffer first. In the converter block return .haveData once per input chunk then .noDataNow, and size output with ceil(ratio*frames).
4. [high] iOS 17 phones collapse tabs 5–8 under a system More that collides with the app's own More tab
   why: Confirmed ContentView.swift:148-179: legacyTabView emits 8 Tabs with no compact-width gating. On iPhone the classic UIKit TabView shows 5 items and pushes the rest (learn, phrases, stats, AND the app's .more) into the OS More list. Deployment target was just lowered to iOS 17 (commit 82130c4), so this is live for all iOS 17 users — a confusing double-More.
   fix: Cap iPhone to ≤5 primary tabs (Translate, Photo, Vocabulary, Learn, More) and fold History (already duplicated in More), Phrases, and Stats into More or their parent screens. Drive both compact and regular layouts from one AppTab source.
5. [medium] Screenshot stitching reads pixels with the wrong bytesPerRow, corrupting overlap detection
   why: getPixelData renders into a context whose stride is 4*width (no padding) but findOverlapHeight indexes that buffer using the ORIGINAL CGImage's bytesPerRow (often padded to 16/32/64-byte alignment). Every row offset is wrong; the bounds guard then silently skips most comparisons, so overlap detection is effectively broken and stitched screenshots mis-join.
   fix: Return and use the same stride the buffer was allocated with (4*width) inside findOverlapHeight; never mix the source CGImage's bytesPerRow with a freshly-rendered 4*width buffer. Only scan the overlap strip rather than allocating full-image buffers for both images.
6. [medium] Vision OCR runs synchronously on the MainActor and silently drops images on non-vision providers
   why: PhotoTextRecognitionService is @MainActor and calls handler.perform([request]) synchronously, so accurate-level OCR on a tall stitched screenshot blocks the main thread for seconds. Separately, cleanupRecognizedText/extractVocabulary pass imageData without checking provider.supportsVision; deepseek/minimax fall back to the text model and CloudAIService strips the image entirely, so vision tasks silently run text-only.
   fix: Make the Vision perform nonisolated/off-actor and hop back to MainActor only to publish results. Gate image paths on provider.supportsVision (reuse gradingProvider()); only pass imageData to chat() when the resolved provider actually supports vision.
7. [medium] CSV import corrupts any entry whose quoted field contains a newline
   why: parseCSVImport pre-splits the whole file on newlines, but export quotes embedded newlines into a single multi-physical-line field. On re-import the splitter shreds that record, parseCSVLine sees unbalanced quotes, and the row is dropped or mangled — backup/restore is lossy for any multi-line definition.
   fix: Replace with an RFC 4180 state-machine parser that tracks quote state across physical line boundaries (accumulate until quotes balance). Add a golden round-trip test: export a term whose definition contains a newline/comma/quote, re-import, assert equality.
8. [medium] Spaced-repetition scheduling is structurally wrong and the correct code is dead
   why: getCardsForReview/getDueCards (due-ordering + 20-card cap) have ZERO call sites; sessions are built by filteredStudyCards in raw deck order with no cap, so a 500-word deck becomes one 500-card session and 'Due for Review' shows due cards unordered. recordReview re-derives previousInterval from dates (collapses to ~1 day after a lapse, so intervals never grow), and quality 2 ('Difficult') is silently counted as INCORRECT. LearningCard.id is the Chinese string, so built-in and vocabulary cards collide in the progress dictionary and English-direction cards with empty Chinese all map to id=='', sharing one bucket.
   fix: Route reloadSessionCards through getCardsForReview(from:limit:). Persist a real interval/lapses on CardProgress (SM-2 style) instead of re-deriving from dates. Give cards a stable namespaced id ('builtin:<chinese>' / 'vocab:<SavedTerm.id>'). Decide explicitly whether 'Difficult' passes or lapses and make the thresholds agree.
9. [medium] Workbook grading and other power features are nearly undiscoverable
   why: Confirmed: WorkbookGradingView is presented from exactly one place (PhotoTranslateView.swift:210) and has no top-level tab, no More entry, and no Shortcuts route. Camera scanner and screenshot translation are reachable only via App Intents; vocabulary import/export is macOS-only. A paid-vision-call feature that users will want to revisit is hidden, and grading results are lost on dismiss (no persistence).
   fix: Add a discoverable entry (primary/overflow action on Photo, plus a More hub row), persist gradings in a GradingHistoryStore (timestamp, score, questions, thumbnail) with a history list, and surface import/export on iOS. Add an onboarding tip pointing to Learn/Workbook.
10. [medium] Strict concurrency checking is off, so the audio data races compile clean
   why: SWIFT_STRICT_CONCURRENCY is unset (Swift 5 mode) and Speech/AVFoundation are @preconcurrency-imported, so the genuinely off-actor buffer/converter/completion-handler races are never checked by the compiler — exactly the code where the use-after-free lives.
   fix: Set SWIFT_STRICT_CONCURRENCY = complete on Debug, triage the warnings (they land on the audio tap/converter/continuation paths), then move toward Swift 6 mode. This converts the latent races into compile-time errors.

=== ARCHITECTURE RECOMMENDATIONS ===
1. Versioned, resilient persistence layer with batch APIs and off-main encoding
   Wrap every store payload in {schemaVersion:Int, data:T}; on load switch on version to run incremental migrators and decode new fields with decodeIfPresent defaults. Add loadCollection that decodes [FailableDecodable<Element>] so one bad row never drops the array. Add addMany/replaceAll and a withBatch{} that suspends the didSet save() until completion (kills the O(n²) save amplification on import). Make save() nonisolated/debounced so large JSON encodes leave the MainActor, and consider moving the larger collections (vocabulary, history, progress) to a JSON file in Application Support instead of UserDefaults.
   benefit: Eliminates the single biggest risk (silent data loss on update), bounds corruption to truly-bad rows, removes main-thread hitches and import jank, and gives a clean path for every future model change.
2. Collapse to a 5-tab frequency-ordered IA with one real More hub
   Primary iPhone tabs: Translate, Photo, Vocabulary, Learn, More. Fold History into a single canonical screen in More (delete the duplicate HistoryView/HistoryRow in MoreView.swift:66-163 and route to HistoryTabView), reach Stats from inside Learn/More (remove the duplicate Stats tab and the in-Learn LearningStatsSheet), and move Phrases under a Library grouping. Give StatsView its own NavigationStack for consistent nav chrome. Drive compact and regular layouts from one AppTab source.
   benefit: Resolves the iOS 17 system-More overflow and the double-More collision, removes the History and Stats duplications, frees tab slots, and gives a frequency-ordered IA that matches real usage.
3. One source of truth for learning/translation direction
   Introduce a resolved ResolvedTranslation { chinese, english, engineDirection } produced once per completed translation, and a LearningContext { nativeIsChinese, learningIsChinese, isBilingual } owned by AppPreferences and derived from learnerMode, with LocalizationManager syncing UI language to it bidirectionally. Route history recording, ruby rendering, term-saving, AI explanation language, pinyin gating, and narration through these instead of re-deriving direction three different ways (UI toggle vs detected content vs per-text containsChinese).
   benefit: Directly fixes the history-direction corruption bug and the inert .bilingual mode, eliminates the App-Language/Learner-Mode divergence, and removes a whole class of direction bugs by construction.
4. Centralize AI provider capability gating into one resolver
   Add a ResolvedRequest factory that, given a task (text/vision/json) and current settings, returns a validated (provider, model, capabilities) tuple or a precise error. Route grading, OCR cleanup, vocabulary extraction, and explanation through it so supportsVision and JSON-mode checks live in one place. Add per-model request shaping (isReasoningModel, tokenParameterName, supportsTemperature) so o3/o4-mini get max_completion_tokens and omit temperature, and harden the Ollama Model.ID force-unwraps into guards.
   benefit: Stops silent image-dropping on non-vision providers, fixes the HTTP-400 on default reasoning models, removes crash-on-bad-Ollama-model, and makes capability handling testable and uniform.
5. A single TranslationBackend service that owns the iOS 17/18/26 availability matrix
   Expose one actor with translate(_:from:to:) and translateBatch that internally picks system-26 / SwiftUI permission-task / AI fallback, plus an incrementing requestID/token so stale translationTask closures self-cancel instead of relying on post-hoc snapshot guards. Route TranslateView, LiveSpeechTranslationView, WordTranslationService, ScreenshotTranslationStore, and the Intents through it; add in-flight de-duplication keyed by cacheKey.
   benefit: Removes duplicated, already-drifting availability gates (some at 18, some at 26), makes the unofficial-API risk fixable in one place, gives clean cancellation, and lets iOS 18–25 use fast batch translation instead of the serial AI fallback.
6. Unify settings into one declarative cross-platform definition and prune dead controls
   Define settings as data (key, type, range, label, footer, platform availability, implemented?) and render Form sections on iOS and a TabView on macOS from that single source. Either implement or remove the ~13 dead macOS toggles (launch-at-login, menu-bar, global hotkey, reminders, chineseFont, fontSize, compactMode, etc.); wire fontSize to a Dynamic-Type scale and chineseFont into RubyTextView if kept. Replace the placeholder App Store ID id123456789 and the apple.com/privacy link with real values.
   benefit: Guarantees iOS/macOS parity automatically, stops advertising non-functional features, and removes embarrassing placeholders before App Store submission.

   fix: Thread the detected direction through: compute actualDirection = detectedTranslationDirection in performTranslation/triggerAITranslation and pass that (not sharedState.direction) to both the guard comparison and handleCompletedTranslation's direction: argument. Keep the source-text snapshot guard.
3. [high] Audio tap captures a non-Sendable AVAudioPCMBuffer into a per-buffer Task (use-after-free + reordered/garbled audio)
   why: SpeechRecognitionService.swift:440-446 spawns Task { await self.processAudioBuffer(buffer) } per tap callback. AVAudioEngine reclaims that buffer once the closure returns, so the async read touches recycled memory; tens of unstructured Tasks/sec hop to the MainActor with no FIFO guarantee (frames reorder), and in-flight Tasks outlive stop()/removeTap, yielding into a finished continuation. Separately the sample-rate converter input block (lines 473-476) always returns the same buffer with .haveData, so the converter can loop/duplicate frames and never signals end-of-stream.
   fix: Do conversion synchronously inside the tap and call inputContinuation?.yield(...) directly (the continuation is Sendable/thread-safe); never spawn a Task per buffer. If a hop is unavoidable, deep-copy the buffer first. In the converter block return .haveData once per input chunk then .noDataNow, and size output with ceil(ratio*frames).
4. [high] iOS 17 phones collapse tabs 5–8 under a system More that collides with the app's own More tab
   why: Confirmed ContentView.swift:148-179: legacyTabView emits 8 Tabs with no compact-width gating. On iPhone the classic UIKit TabView shows 5 items and pushes the rest (learn, phrases, stats, AND the app's .more) into the OS More list. Deployment target was just lowered to iOS 17 (commit 82130c4), so this is live for all iOS 17 users — a confusing double-More.
   fix: Cap iPhone to ≤5 primary tabs (Translate, Photo, Vocabulary, Learn, More) and fold History (already duplicated in More), Phrases, and Stats into More or their parent screens. Drive both compact and regular layouts from one AppTab source.
5. [medium] Screenshot stitching reads pixels with the wrong bytesPerRow, corrupting overlap detection
   why: getPixelData renders into a context whose stride is 4*width (no padding) but findOverlapHeight indexes that buffer using the ORIGINAL CGImage's bytesPerRow (often padded to 16/32/64-byte alignment). Every row offset is wrong; the bounds guard then silently skips most comparisons, so overlap detection is effectively broken and stitched screenshots mis-join.
   fix: Return and use the same stride the buffer was allocated with (4*width) inside findOverlapHeight; never mix the source CGImage's bytesPerRow with a freshly-rendered 4*width buffer. Only scan the overlap strip rather than allocating full-image buffers for both images.
6. [medium] Vision OCR runs synchronously on the MainActor and silently drops images on non-vision providers
   why: PhotoTextRecognitionService is @MainActor and calls handler.perform([request]) synchronously, so accurate-level OCR on a tall stitched screenshot blocks the main thread for seconds. Separately, cleanupRecognizedText/extractVocabulary pass imageData without checking provider.supportsVision; deepseek/minimax fall back to the text model and CloudAIService strips the image entirely, so vision tasks silently run text-only.
   fix: Make the Vision perform nonisolated/off-actor and hop back to MainActor only to publish results. Gate image paths on provider.supportsVision (reuse gradingProvider()); only pass imageData to chat() when the resolved provider actually supports vision.
7. [medium] CSV import corrupts any entry whose quoted field contains a newline
   why: parseCSVImport pre-splits the whole file on newlines, but export quotes embedded newlines into a single multi-physical-line field. On re-import the splitter shreds that record, parseCSVLine sees unbalanced quotes, and the row is dropped or mangled — backup/restore is lossy for any multi-line definition.
   fix: Replace with an RFC 4180 state-machine parser that tracks quote state across physical line boundaries (accumulate until quotes balance). Add a golden round-trip test: export a term whose definition contains a newline/comma/quote, re-import, assert equality.
8. [medium] Spaced-repetition scheduling is structurally wrong and the correct code is dead
   why: getCardsForReview/getDueCards (due-ordering + 20-card cap) have ZERO call sites; sessions are built by filteredStudyCards in raw deck order with no cap, so a 500-word deck becomes one 500-card session and 'Due for Review' shows due cards unordered. recordReview re-derives previousInterval from dates (collapses to ~1 day after a lapse, so intervals never grow), and quality 2 ('Difficult') is silently counted as INCORRECT. LearningCard.id is the Chinese string, so built-in and vocabulary cards collide in the progress dictionary and English-direction cards with empty Chinese all map to id=='', sharing one bucket.
   fix: Route reloadSessionCards through getCardsForReview(from:limit:). Persist a real interval/lapses on CardProgress (SM-2 style) instead of re-deriving from dates. Give cards a stable namespaced id ('builtin:<chinese>' / 'vocab:<SavedTerm.id>'). Decide explicitly whether 'Difficult' passes or lapses and make the thresholds agree.
9. [medium] Workbook grading and other power features are nearly undiscoverable
   why: Confirmed: WorkbookGradingView is presented from exactly one place (PhotoTranslateView.swift:210) and has no top-level tab, no More entry, and no Shortcuts route. Camera scanner and screenshot translation are reachable only via App Intents; vocabulary import/export is macOS-only. A paid-vision-call feature that users will want to revisit is hidden, and grading results are lost on dismiss (no persistence).
   fix: Add a discoverable entry (primary/overflow action on Photo, plus a More hub row), persist gradings in a GradingHistoryStore (timestamp, score, questions, thumbnail) with a history list, and surface import/export on iOS. Add an onboarding tip pointing to Learn/Workbook.
10. [medium] Strict concurrency checking is off, so the audio data races compile clean
   why: SWIFT_STRICT_CONCURRENCY is unset (Swift 5 mode) and Speech/AVFoundation are @preconcurrency-imported, so the genuinely off-actor buffer/converter/completion-handler races are never checked by the compiler — exactly the code where the use-after-free lives.
   fix: Set SWIFT_STRICT_CONCURRENCY = complete on Debug, triage the warnings (they land on the audio tap/converter/continuation paths), then move toward Swift 6 mode. This converts the latent races into compile-time errors.

=== ARCHITECTURE RECOMMENDATIONS ===
1. Versioned, resilient persistence layer with batch APIs and off-main encoding
   Wrap every store payload in {schemaVersion:Int, data:T}; on load switch on version to run incremental migrators and decode new fields with decodeIfPresent defaults. Add loadCollection that decodes [FailableDecodable<Element>] so one bad row never drops the array. Add addMany/replaceAll and a withBatch{} that suspends the didSet save() until completion (kills the O(n²) save amplification on import). Make save() nonisolated/debounced so large JSON encodes leave the MainActor, and consider moving the larger collections (vocabulary, history, progress) to a JSON file in Application Support instead of UserDefaults.
   benefit: Eliminates the single biggest risk (silent data loss on update), bounds corruption to truly-bad rows, removes main-thread hitches and import jank, and gives a clean path for every future model change.
2. Collapse to a 5-tab frequency-ordered IA with one real More hub
   Primary iPhone tabs: Translate, Photo, Vocabulary, Learn, More. Fold History into a single canonical screen in More (delete the duplicate HistoryView/HistoryRow in MoreView.swift:66-163 and route to HistoryTabView), reach Stats from inside Learn/More (remove the duplicate Stats tab and the in-Learn LearningStatsSheet), and move Phrases under a Library grouping. Give StatsView its own NavigationStack for consistent nav chrome. Drive compact and regular layouts from one AppTab source.
   benefit: Resolves the iOS 17 system-More overflow and the double-More collision, removes the History and Stats duplications, frees tab slots, and gives a frequency-ordered IA that matches real usage.
3. One source of truth for learning/translation direction
   Introduce a resolved ResolvedTranslation { chinese, english, engineDirection } produced once per completed translation, and a LearningContext { nativeIsChinese, learningIsChinese, isBilingual } owned by AppPreferences and derived from learnerMode, with LocalizationManager syncing UI language to it bidirectionally. Route history recording, ruby rendering, term-saving, AI explanation language, pinyin gating, and narration through these instead of re-deriving direction three different ways (UI toggle vs detected content vs per-text containsChinese).
   benefit: Directly fixes the history-direction corruption bug and the inert .bilingual mode, eliminates the App-Language/Learner-Mode divergence, and removes a whole class of direction bugs by construction.
4. Centralize AI provider capability gating into one resolver
   Add a ResolvedRequest factory that, given a task (text/vision/json) and current settings, returns a validated (provider, model, capabilities) tuple or a precise error. Route grading, OCR cleanup, vocabulary extraction, and explanation through it so supportsVision and JSON-mode checks live in one place. Add per-model request shaping (isReasoningModel, tokenParameterName, supportsTemperature) so o3/o4-mini get max_completion_tokens and omit temperature, and harden the Ollama Model.ID force-unwraps into guards.
   benefit: Stops silent image-dropping on non-vision providers, fixes the HTTP-400 on default reasoning models, removes crash-on-bad-Ollama-model, and makes capability handling testable and uniform.
5. A single TranslationBackend service that owns the iOS 17/18/26 availability matrix
   Expose one actor with translate(_:from:to:) and translateBatch that internally picks system-26 / SwiftUI permission-task / AI fallback, plus an incrementing requestID/token so stale translationTask closures self-cancel instead of relying on post-hoc snapshot guards. Route TranslateView, LiveSpeechTranslationView, WordTranslationService, ScreenshotTranslationStore, and the Intents through it; add in-flight de-duplication keyed by cacheKey.
   benefit: Removes duplicated, already-drifting availability gates (some at 18, some at 26), makes the unofficial-API risk fixable in one place, gives clean cancellation, and lets iOS 18–25 use fast batch translation instead of the serial AI fallback.
6. Unify settings into one declarative cross-platform definition and prune dead controls
   Define settings as data (key, type, range, label, footer, platform availability, implemented?) and render Form sections on iOS and a TabView on macOS from that single source. Either implement or remove the ~13 dead macOS toggles (launch-at-login, menu-bar, global hotkey, reminders, chineseFont, fontSize, compactMode, etc.); wire fontSize to a Dynamic-Type scale and chineseFont into RubyTextView if kept. Replace the placeholder App Store ID id123456789 and the apple.com/privacy link with real values.
   benefit: Guarantees iOS/macOS parity automatically, stops advertising non-functional features, and removes embarrassing placeholders before App Store submission.

=== WORKFLOW ENHANCEMENTS ===
1. Make spaced repetition real and visible: Wire the existing due-ordering builder into sessions, add a configurable session size (10/20/50/All) in the Learn menu, and persist a proper SM-2 record (interval, repetitions, ease, lapses) on CardProgress so intervals grow from real history. 2. Persist and reopen workbook gradings as a study source: Add a GradingHistoryStore (Codable GradingRecord: timestamp, score, summary, questions, optional thumbnail) and a history list that reopens past results into the same GradedQuestionCard UI. Reconcile the displayed score with the computed correct/total so the headline can't contradict the cards.
3. Streaming + cancellation across explanation, translation, and grading: Add an SSE-streaming variant of CloudAIService.chat (and reuse OllamaService.chatStream) so the explanation/translation/grading UIs render tokens as they arrive with natural cancellation and a Cancel button — instead of a spinner that can sit for up to 180s. Show per-image upload progress for multi-page workbook grading.
4. Photo OCR pipeline that is fast, correct, and resumable: Downsample images before OCR with a max-pixel budget (cap the long edge ~4000px via CGImageSourceCreateThumbnail), route every entry point (PhotosPicker, fileImporter, drop, camera) through one cancellable processImage(token:) flow so the newest selection always wins, surface low-confidence blocks with topCandidates(3) for tap-to-correct, and write the OCR draft to disk before translation so a jetsam kill during stitching doesn't lose the work. On iOS 18+ adopt the async RecognizeTextRequest to drop the main-thread perform and double-resume hazard.
5. Discoverability and continuity for the whole app: Add primary/overflow actions on Translate and Photo for camera scan and screenshot translation, surface vocabulary import/export on iOS, persist the selected tab via @SceneStorage so the app reopens where the user left off, and add a first-run tour pointing to Learn and Workbook grading. 54	
55	### Executive summary
56	
57	SwiftMandarin is a feature-rich, ambitious SwiftUI Mandarin-learning app whose breadth (8 tabs, 10-provider AI abstraction, on-device + cloud translation, photo OCR, screenshot stitching, workbook grading, spaced repetition, bilingual UI) outpaces the robustness of its foundations. The codebase is functional but carries three structural risks that should be treated as release-blockers. (1) PERSISTENCE FRAGILITY: every persisted model uses synthesized Codable with no CodingKeys, no schemaVersion, and no defaulting (confirmed by grep across Models/). The PersistentCodableStore .backup is the SAME schema, so any future non-optional field throws keyNotFound on BOTH decode paths and silently wipes all user vocabulary/progress/history on update. Collection decode is all-or-nothing, so one corrupt row drops the whole array. This is the single highest-leverage area to harden. (3) IA/DISCOVERABILITY DEBT: on the now-live iOS 17 path the legacy TabView emits 8 tabs with no compact-width gating (confirmed ContentView.swift:148-179), so tabs 5-8 — including the app's OWN More tab — collapse under the system More overflow, a confusing collision. The genuinely valuable workbook-grading feature is reachable through exactly one buried sheet (PhotoTranslateView.swift:210) and nothing else. The More tab is a 601-line catch-all with a duplicate divergent History screen, dead settings, a placeholder App Store ID, and a privacy link pointing at apple.com. Strategically, the app is one solid refactor of the data layer, the information architecture, and a unified translation/learning-direction model away from being genuinely excellent. Concurrency safety is also unverified by the compiler (SWIFT_STRICT_CONCURRENCY is unset), masking the audio races. Recommend: freeze new features, ship the persistence envelope + the history-direction fix + the audio-buffer fix first, then execute the IA consolidation (5 tabs + real More hub) and a single source-of-truth learning-direction model.
58	
59	### Top prioritized issues
60	
61	**B1. [CRITICAL] Schema evolution will silently wipe all user data on the next model change**  
62	- *Why:* All persisted models (SavedTerm, CardProgress, DailyActivity, history) use synthesized Codable with no schemaVersion/CodingKeys/decode defaults (verified: grep finds none in Models/). PersistentCodableStore.load decodes the whole collection at once and the .backup is the same schema, so adding any non-optional stored property throws keyNotFound on BOTH the primary and backup decode, and load() returns nil — every saved word, flashcard, streak, and history entry is dropped on update. One corrupt element also discards the entire array.  
63	- *Fix:* Introduce a versioned envelope {schemaVersion:Int, data:T} in save/load. Decode tolerantly: give new fields explicit decodeIfPresent defaults via custom init(from:), and add a per-element resilient decoder (decode [FailableDecodable<Element>], keep successes, log/drop only the truly-corrupt rows). Ship this BEFORE any further model changes so existing 0.x payloads survive the upgrade.
64	
65	**B2. [HIGH] History records the UI-toggle direction, not the translated direction — corrupts every cross-direction entry**  
66	- *Why:* Confirmed: triggerTranslation computes actualDirection = detectedTranslationDirection from input content (TranslateView.swift:889), but performTranslation (line 959) and triggerAITranslation (line 923) snapshot directionSnapshot = sharedState.direction (the UI toggle) and write THAT into handleCompletedTranslation (line 975). When the toggle says EN→中 but the user types Chinese, the engine correctly returns English yet history stores direction=englishToChinese. TranslationHistoryEntry.chineseText/.englishText key off direction, so source and target are mislabeled through History, restore, and any term saved from a restored entry.  
67	- *Fix:* Thread the detected direction through: compute actualDirection = detectedTranslationDirection in performTranslation/triggerAITranslation and pass that (not sharedState.direction) to both the guard comparison and handleCompletedTranslation's direction: argument. Keep the source-text snapshot guard.
68	
69	**B3. [HIGH] Audio tap captures a non-Sendable AVAudioPCMBuffer into a per-buffer Task (use-after-free + reordered/garbled audio)**  
70	- *Why:* SpeechRecognitionService.swift:440-446 spawns Task { await self.processAudioBuffer(buffer) } per tap callback. AVAudioEngine reclaims that buffer once the closure returns, so the async read touches recycled memory; tens of unstructured Tasks/sec hop to the MainActor with no FIFO guarantee (frames reorder), and in-flight Tasks outlive stop()/removeTap, yielding into a finished continuation. Separately the sample-rate converter input block (lines 473-476) always returns the same buffer with .haveData, so the converter can loop/duplicate frames and never signals end-of-stream.

Here's where things stand:

## ✅ Implemented (Photo-tab workbook suite + analytics + More declutter)

**1. Direct camera capture** — `CameraImagePicker.swift` (`UIImagePickerController(.camera)`); a prominent **拍照 · Camera** button now sits beside Photos/Files in the grader, auto-hidden on macOS/Simulator/camera-less devices.

**2. Question database (review bank)** — `WorkbookBank.swift` with `WorkbookQuestion` + `WorkbookQuestionBankStore`. Each graded question has **Add to Bank**; results have **Add all to Bank**.

A second workflow (4 reviewers → independent verifiers) reviewed only the new/changed code. **7 confirmed / 6 refuted.** All 7 fixed:
- **Re-grade duplication (med/high, the key regression):** after a successful grade the button stayed live with the same photos loaded, so re-tapping wrote a duplicate `GradedSession`, a duplicate on-disk photo copy, and double-counted `questionsGraded`. Fixed: `canGrade` now requires `!didSaveSession`; `grade()` guards `!isGrading && !didSaveSession`; `onChange(of:)` the image arrays resets the flag so editing inputs re-enables a fresh grade.

+- **Partial image-save feedback (low):** if some scans fail to write, `grade()` now surfaces a non-fatal "N scan(s) couldn't be saved to history" notice (the grade result is unaffected).

+- **Bulk "Add all to Bank" feedback (low):** the grader's bulk button now flips to *Added all* and disables; the history detail's "Add all" is now **content-derived** (`allInBank` from bank membership) instead of a one-shot flag, so it reflects items already banked.
+- **Heatmap detail crowding (low):** the 4-metric + date row now scales the metric counts (`minimumScaleFactor`) and pins the date (`layoutPriority`/`fixedSize`) so nothing clips on iPhone SE/mini.
+- **Concurrency:** `WorkbookImageStore` marked `nonisolated` (the project defaults to MainActor isolation) so its file IO runs off-main from detached tasks with zero warnings.
